o1.biggest_strength: RTO cost is split by pincode group with per-order refusal math that justifies tiered discounts and calls, and the holdout is built in.
o1.biggest_mistake: T4 (prepaid switch) is submitted as Marketing but the body carries a ₹20/₹40 discount that only works after Confirm, which risks Meta rejecting or recategorising it, and the discount is never sized against margin.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the prepaid and cart templates clean Marketing with the incentive properly sized and the STOP footer on every template, and put the after-hours bot menu live before chats are rerouted.

o2.biggest_strength: The reply scripts are the most usable part: short, light Hinglish, and clearly mapped to the five real questions with an after-hours menu.
o2.biggest_mistake: Template 3 is filed as Utility but tries to switch COD buyers to prepaid with a UPI link, which is Marketing and will be recategorised or rejected, and the 7-day exchange claim is stated as fact without the store's real policy.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Get the categories right (template 3 as Marketing, template 1 as Utility without any payment link), make the exchange wording an assumption rather than a fact, and show the money behind each move like Output 1 does.

reason: Output 1 would actually cut RTOs, because it splits the discount by pincode risk and shows the refusal cost per order, and its metric table maps straight to a weekly scorecard. Output 2 has clearer scripts and a smarter after-hours plan, but its Utility prepaid template and the unverified exchange promise are exactly the kind of mistakes that get templates rejected and customers annoyed.
